input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The OR composition checks for retry_all when deciding whether to flatten an existing retry_any.
- failure path: with `(A & B) | C`, the retry_all on the left is spliced into the retry_any as if it were a plain list of predicates, so the combination behaves as `A | B | C`: a retry fires when only A holds although the author required A and B together; no error is raised and the extra retries are silent

Reviewer finding
- description: In the async retry_any.__ror__, the flatten check tests isinstance(other, retry_all) instead of retry_any, so a left-hand retry_all is merged into the retry_any.
- rationale: Trigger: an async retry_all as the left operand of |, e.g. all_cond | any_cond, which dispatches to any_cond.__ror__(all_cond). The check passes, so the result is retry_any(*all_cond.retries, *any_cond.retries), i.e. any(a, b, c) instead of any(all(a, b), c). Impact: the retry predicate silently changes meaning and retries under conditions it should not, or fails to retry when it should.
critique: Both describe the same bug. The OR composition flattens when it sees a retry_all instead of a retry_any, so a left-hand retry_all gets spliced in and (A&B)|C becomes A|B|C. The finding names the same wrong isinstance check and the same silent change in meaning.
